text:
Michael Carcone was never drafted and worked his way up through the AHL to become a regular in Utah. His season has been stop and start: 13 games, a long absence between Oct. 8 and Nov. 1, and 12.3 minutes a night on the bottom of the lineup.

The scoring hasn't come. He has 1 goal and 3 points, with 27 shots on goal, shooting 3.7%. His 2.3 expected goals (the quality of his chances) suggest he should have one or two more, and Utah has scored 2.4 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. In his last ten games he has 1 point where we'd expect about 3.6.

His five-on-five numbers are good: Utah takes 56.6% of the expected goals with him on. Evolving-Hockey liked his play-driving last season too, putting his impact on chances created in the 95th percentile among forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags a signature: 18% of his setups come from behind the net, more than twice the typical forward.

He scored 16 goals last season. Seven shots against Boston and six against St. Louis say he is still finding the net; watch whether the puck starts going in.
